title: rethrows: Your Own map
hints: A `rethrows` function only throws when the closure you pass it throws.
Loop over `self`, call `try transform(element)`, and collect the results.
`for element in self { out.append(try transform(element)) }` — then `(try? words.myMap(parse)) != nil`.
jsBridge: `rethrows` says "I only throw if the closure you gave me throws", so `map` with a non-throwing closure needs no `try`. JS doesn't track this; every call may throw.

compass.q: In JS, `arr.map(f)` might throw if `f` throws, and nothing tells you. How does `rethrows` encode that in the type?
